brute_force.name: SSH / Authentication Brute Force
brute_force.description: Repeated failed login attempts to gain unauthorised access.
detection_indicators: High volume of failed authentication events (rule IDs 5760, 5763, 5503, 5504)
Same source IP targeting one or multiple accounts
Spike in 'PAM: User login failed' or 'sshd: brute force' alerts
investigation_steps: Use query_recent_alerts on the source IP to count failed attempts and time span.
Use check_successful_login to see if any later succeeded.
Check IP reputation (check_ip_reputation) – look for VT malicious > 0 or abuse score > 50.
If source IP is 0.0.0.0 (missing), use query_alerts_by_target to find candidate attacker IPs.
Determine if target user is privileged (root, admin, etc.) for severity escalation.
response_actions: If >10 failed attempts in 24h OR any successful login after failures → confirmed threat.
Block source IP for 3600 seconds (CRITICAL severity).
If source is internal and not a known security tool, still block for 3600s and escalate.
Escalate to Tier‑2 analyst with CRITICAL priority, summarising failed/successful counts.
brute_force.escalation_requirements: Always escalate after blocking; escalate even without blocking if the pattern is suspicious but not yet confirmed (MEDIUM priority).

privilege_escalation.name: Privilege Escalation (General)
privilege_escalation.description: Successful or attempted elevation of privileges (sudo, su, kernel exploit, UAC bypass).
detection_indicators: Alert rules: 5400, 5401 (failed sudo), 5402, 5403 (successful sudo), 5404 (new sudo session)
Unexpected process creation as root from a non‑privileged parent
investigation_steps: If the alert lacks a source IP (0.0.0.0), use query_alerts_by_target on the target host to find who was recently attacking.
Look for preceding brute‑force or suspicious login from the same host using query_recent_alerts.
Check if the escalation was performed by a known admin during business hours (use get_asset_info and context).
If linked to a network attack, the attacker IP is likely the source of the preceding brute force.
response_actions: If the escalation is linked to an external attacker IP: block that IP for 3600s and escalate CRITICAL.
If the escalation appears to be from a local exploit (e.g., kernel bug) with no network attacker, consider host isolation (via disable_user_account or manual action).
If performed by a trusted admin during business hours from a whitelisted IP, close as FP (use close_alert_as_fp).
In all confirmed cases, escalate to Tier‑2 analyst with a detailed timeline.
privilege_escalation.escalation_requirements: Escalate immediately if linked to an attacker; also escalate if uncertain but high potential impact.

port_scan.name: Network Port Scan
port_scan.description: Reconnaissance activity – single IP connecting to many ports or many hosts.
detection_indicators: Multiple firewall deny events from same source to multiple ports
investigation_steps: Check if source IP is an authorised vulnerability scanner (check asset inventory).
Use query_recent_alerts to see the diversity of targets and ports.
Check IP reputation – known scanner IPs often appear in threat intel.
response_actions: If external and not authorised: block for 3600s and escalate with HIGH priority.
If internal and not a known scanner: isolate host and escalate to investigate possible compromise.
port_scan.escalation_requirements: Escalate for any confirmed unauthorised scan.

lateral_movement.name: Lateral Movement
lateral_movement.description: Attacker moving from one compromised host to another within the network.
detection_indicators: Successful authentications (rule 5501, 5502) from the same source IP on multiple distinct hosts within a short time.
Privileged account usage on hosts that don't normally require it.
investigation_steps: Identify the source IP and verify its asset criticality.
Check if the movement originates from a domain controller or high‑value asset.
Correlate with earlier brute‑force or privilege escalation events.
response_actions: Block source IP immediately on all detected targets.
Escalate CRITICAL – isolate affected hosts if feasible.
lateral_movement.escalation_requirements: Always escalate when lateral movement is confirmed.
